diagnosis: Only one check failed across all rollouts: C1 in rollout_index 1. Failure mode: ENCODING MISMATCH. In rollout 1, PF1 was properly revealed by A2 at turn 4 ("The gateway can translate those requests to v2 only when compatibility traffic is capped at exactly 120 requests per minute per tenant") and was correctly cited in justification_fact_ids ("PF1", "PF2"). The settlement's decisions reflect an attempt to use PF1: proxy_enabled=true, proxy_request_cap_per_tenant=120, and a compatibility_plan commitment reading "Enable gateway proxy translation for SDK 4.8 v1 requests to v2 with a cap of 120 requests per minute per tenant." The only field that could have failed C1 is deprecation_mode, which was set to "guided". In the three passing rollouts, C1 accepted deprecation_mode values of "phased with proxy support" (rollout 0), "v1 disabled July 1 with gateway compatibility translation and guided migration support" (rollout 2), and "proxy-assisted" (rollout 3) — all of which explicitly reference the proxy/translation/compatibility approach. The value "guided" in rollout 1 describes the migration support side (from PF2) but omits any reference to the proxy/translation/compatibility mode that PF1 is supposed to flip the decision toward. The model had the right information and used it in the proxy-related fields and commitments, but the deprecation_mode field name itself was filled with a value that only captures the PF2-driven half of the decision, not the PF1-driven mode change. This is an encoding mismatch: the check expects deprecation_mode to encode the compatibility-proxy/translation mode, but the model reasonably used "guided" as a shorthand that collapses both facts into a single label without naming the proxy dimension. No other checks failed in any rollout. No rollout hit the turn cap (turn counts: 5, 8, 10, 6; auto_failed_count=0). No TELEPATHY, NEVER REVEALED, REVEALED BUT UNUSED, or MISAPPLIED failures are present in the data.

C1.why: The public draft supports direct disablement; PF1 changes the mode to a compatibility proxy or translation approach, enables it, and sets its tenant limit to exactly 120 requests per minute.

fix_instructions: C1 (linked to PF1, owner A2): ENCODING MISMATCH. The check C1 gates the deprecation_mode field and requires it to reflect PF1's flip from direct disablement to a compatibility proxy/translation approach. The model in rollout 1 set deprecation_mode to "guided" — a value that captures the PF2-driven guided-migration support but omits the proxy/translation dimension PF1 is supposed to introduce. The three passing rollouts used values containing explicit proxy/translation language ("phased with proxy support", "v1 disabled July 1 with gateway compatibility translation and guided migration support", "proxy-assisted"). Loosen C1's accepted-value matching for deprecation_mode to accept any value that contains at least one of the substrings "proxy", "translation", or "compatibility" (case-insensitive), rather than requiring an exact or near-exact string. This would accept all four observed values except "guided", which correctly fails because it lacks any proxy/translation/compatibility token. Flag: this loosening does NOT risk a LEAKED regression because the public draft supports direct disablement and a lone decision-maker without PF1 would have no reason to introduce proxy/translation/compatibility language into deprecation_mode — those terms come specifically from PF1's disclosure of the gateway translation capability. Do not change PF1's text, shared_context, or any other check; all other checks (C2–C6, P1) passed in all four rollouts and must be left untouched.
